top_choice_rationale: Base editing is a defined chemical reaction, in situ deamination of a single nucleobase made programmable by a deaminase-Cas9 nickase fusion, with the cell's repair converting it into a stable base change. The adenine editor needed an evolved DNA adenine deaminase, which is new chemistry rather than a repackaging of 2020 cleavage-based editing. Products are verified at nucleotide resolution, independently reproduced by many laboratories and already used clinically. The Liu, Komor, Gaudelli allocation follows the documented work (concept and both editor families, first cytosine editor, first adenine editor), and the citation is worded around programmable base conversion so the Kondo and Nishida Target-AID priority is acknowledged rather than contradicted. P001 also has the broadest explicit support, five members.
